correctness.rationale: The disjoint coding and strictly decreasing pressure give the unique s in (1/q,1); finite subsystems give the matching Hausdorff lower bound, and the probability is non-atomic as cylinder masses decay uniformly. Conditional on first symbol, the cell mass is exactly c^s[sum_(j>n) j^(−qs)+n^(−qs)Q_lambda(a)], including both endpoints. Reconstructing the tail expansion by Euler–Maclaurin and inserting x=H n^(1−q)+(a−1/2)n^(−q)/Z+O(n^(−q−1)) gives the same leading coefficient and linear correction c^s(a−1/2) in Kx^d. The −1/2 terms cancel and leave c^s(Q_lambda(a)−a); errors are uniform in a, and evaluation at a=lambda makes the order sharp. For t>0 use the same iid letters to count j>n, with at most m w_n probability of any mismatch. Here n is of order m^(1/(qs−1)) at fixed t, so m w_n and the Poisson mean error are O(m^(−1/(qs−1))); Le Cam gives O(m^(−1)). This establishes precisely the stated upper rate, not optimality of the Poisson rate. At t=0 no coded point equals zero almost surely; the survival limit follows from zero visits. Replay: RESULT.md, Eqs. (1)–(3) and proof §4, with the above reconstruction. Frozen verify_endpoint.py was read, not executed, and its two reported local examples do not directly test the TV estimate.
